questions.question: State the law of magnetic poles and explain why repulsion, not attraction, proves that an object is a magnet.
questions.expected_answer: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract. A magnet attracts unmagnetised magnetic materials (e.g. iron) by inducing magnetism in them, so attraction does not prove the object is a magnet. Only a magnet can repel a pole of another magnet.

questions.question: Describe how to show the magnetic field pattern around a bar magnet and describe the pattern.
questions.expected_answer: Place paper over the magnet, sprinkle iron filings and tap gently (or plot with a small compass). The filings form curved lines from the N pole to the S pole, crowded near the poles where the field is strongest.

questions.question: Explain why the magnetic pole near the geographic North Pole is a south magnetic pole, and give one reason the Earth's magnetic field is important to life.
questions.expected_answer: The north-seeking pole of a compass is attracted to it, and unlike poles attract, so it must be a south magnetic pole. The field forms the magnetosphere, which deflects harmful charged particles of the solar wind (also used by animals to navigate).
